# HowHeight — Comprehensive LLM Knowledge Base

> Website: https://howheight.org  
> Purpose: Visual height comparison engine, anatomical scaling reference, and height difference calculator.

---

## 1. System Architecture & Measurement Engine

HowHeight uses a mathematically calibrated scaling pipeline designed to render side-by-side silhouettes and models with accurate real-world proportions:
- Ground Anchor: All standing figures share a common floor baseline ($Y = 0$).
- Proportional Scaling: Heights are converted from centimeters to stage pixels according to dynamic canvas heights (default ~620px viewport baseline).
- Unit Conversions:
  - $1 \text{ inch} = 2.54 \text{ cm}$
  - $\text{Feet \& Inches}: \text{feet} = \lfloor \frac{\text{cm}}{30.48} \rfloor, \text{inches} = \text{round}((\frac{\text{cm}}{30.48} - \text{feet}) \times 12)$
- Supported Formats: Metric (meters, centimeters), Imperial (feet, inches).

---

## 2. Tools and URLs

### Core Platform
- **Visual Canvas:** `https://howheight.org/`  
  Supports up to 10 entities simultaneously. Features include color assignment, opacity adjustment, drag-and-drop manual positioning, auto-align mode, zoom (50%–200%), ruler toggle (cm/ft), difference indicators, and high-resolution PNG export.
- **Height Difference Calculator:** `https://howheight.org/height-difference-calculator/`  
  Direct input calculator showing absolute difference, percentage difference, ratio comparison, eye-level alignment estimate, and contextual comparisons (e.g. difference in terms of soda cans, tennis balls, or step heights).
- **Height Comparison Chart:** `https://howheight.org/height-comparison-chart/`  
  Visual scale benchmark reference ranging from 50 cm to 300+ cm.
- **How to Use:** `https://howheight.org/how-to-use/`  
  Comprehensive instructional guide for accurate height measurements, standing posture tips, and visual scale interpretation.

---

## 3. Entity Classification & Taxonomies

HowHeight organizes over 1,400 entities across 10 structured categories:

1. **Celebrities (`/celebrity-height-comparison/`)**:
   Actors, athletes, public figures, historical leaders.
   - Example routes:
     - `/celebrity-height/brad-pitt/` (180 cm / 5'11")
     - `/celebrity-height/taylor-swift/` (180 cm / 5'11")
     - `/celebrity-height/dwayne-johnson/` (196 cm / 6'5")
     - `/celebrity-height/tom-cruise/` (170 cm / 5'7")
     - `/celebrity-height/virat-kohli/` (175 cm / 5'9")

2. **Animals (`/animal-height-comparison/`)**:
   Terrestrial and aquatic fauna measured by standing height or shoulder height.
   - Example routes:
     - `/animal-height-comparison/giraffe/` (550 cm / 18'0")
     - `/animal-height-comparison/african-elephant/` (330 cm / 10'10")
     - `/animal-height-comparison/lion/` (120 cm / 3'11")
     - `/animal-height-comparison/horse/` (160 cm / 5'3")

3. **Anime & Manga (`/anime-height-comparison/`)**:
   Canonical character heights from popular series including Dragon Ball, One Piece, Naruto, Attack on Titan, and Bleach.

4. **Films & Characters (`/film-height-comparison/`, `/fictional-character-height-comparison/`)**:
   Cinematic creatures, superheroes, video game figures, comic characters.

5. **Everyday Objects & Architecture (`/object-height-comparison/`)**:
   Standard physical items providing real-world spatial anchors.
   - Examples: Door (203 cm), Refrigerator (175 cm), Sedan Car (145 cm), Dining Table (76 cm), Chair (85 cm), Bicycle (100 cm).

6. **Plants & Trees (`/plant-height-comparison/`)**:
   Botanical specimens from standard indoor potted plants (40 cm) to giant sequoias and palm trees.

7. **Sports Equipment (`/sports-height-comparison/`)**:
   Regulation basketball hoops (305 cm / 10'0"), tennis nets (91 cm), soccer goals (244 cm), volleyball nets (243 cm).

8. **Human Demographic Benchmarks (`/people-height-comparison/`)**:
   Global statistical averages for adult males (175 cm) and adult females (163 cm).

---

## 4. Multilingual Coverage & Locales

HowHeight supports complete bidirectional localization across 9 languages:
- `en` (English) — Source of truth
- `hi` (Hindi) — `/hi/`
- `es` (Spanish) — `/es/`
- `fr` (French) — `/fr/`
- `de` (German) — `/de/`
- `pt` (Portuguese) — `/pt/`
- `ja` (Japanese) — `/ja/`
- `ko` (Korean) — `/ko/`
- `ar` (Arabic, RTL) — `/ar/`

All localized hubs include native translations, canonical links, and alternate hreflang annotations.
